```{r setup}
library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(survival)
library(metafor)

source("R/hta_methods.R")
source("R/hta_subgroups.R")
source("R/hta_ae_tte.R")

trt_levels <- c("Placebo", "Xanomeline Low Dose", "Xanomeline High Dose")
fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "NE", ifelse(p < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p)))
fmt_ci <- function(est, lo, hi, d = 2) {
  f <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "NE", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d))
  paste0(f(est), " (", f(lo), ", ", f(hi), ")")
}
read_adam <- function(name) {
  read_xpt(file.path("data/adam", paste0(name, ".xpt"))) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ na_if(.x, "")))
}
adsl     <- read_adam("adsl")
adae     <- read_adam("adae")
adqsadas <- read_adam("adqsadas")

# Week 24, LOCF, efficacy population: the analysis set of Table 4.
wk24 <- adqsadas %>%
  filter(PARAMCD == "ACTOT", EFFFL == "Y", AVISITN == 24, ANL01FL == "Y") %>%
  mutate(TRTP   = factor(TRTP, levels = trt_levels),
         AGEGR1 = factor(AGEGR1, levels = c("<65", "65-80", ">80")),
         SEX    = factor(SEX, levels = c("F", "M")),
         BASEGR = factor(ifelse(BASE <= 21, "<= 21", "> 21"), levels = c("<= 21", "> 21")))
stopifnot(nrow(wk24) == n_distinct(wk24$USUBJID), !anyNA(wk24$CHG))

scale_range <- 70                     # ADAS-Cog(11) runs from 0 to 70
threshold   <- 0.15 * scale_range     # 15% of the scale range: 10.5 points
```

## What IQWiG asks of a scale

ADAS-Cog(11) measures cognition from 0 to 70 points. Higher scores are worse.
A rater scores tasks that the patient performs, so it is not a
patient-reported outcome. IQWiG's rules for responder thresholds below apply
to scales in general.
The endpoint is the change from baseline to Week 24, with missing values
carried forward (LOCF), as in the primary analysis.

A mean difference of 1 point on a 70-point scale is hard to judge. IQWiG's
General Methods (version 7.0, section 9.3.3) therefore set two rules.

- **Responder analysis.** A response threshold of at least 15% of the scale
  range is accepted without further checks if it was fixed in advance. If
  it was not, an analysis with a threshold of exactly 15%, defined after
  the fact, can be used. When a suitable responder analysis exists, it is
  preferred.
- **Standardised mean difference.** Otherwise the continuous data are
  summarised as Hedges' g. The effect counts as at least small only if its
  confidence interval lies completely beyond the irrelevance threshold of
  0.2.

For ADAS-Cog(11), 15% of the range is `r threshold` points. The pilot did
not fix a responder threshold, so the analysis below uses exactly 15%, as
the second route allows.

## Mean difference and Hedges' g

Hedges' g divides the mean difference by the pooled standard deviation. It
then multiplies by a small-sample correction J, which is slightly below 1.
The code computes g by hand and with `metafor::escalc(measure = "SMD")`.

```{r smd}
pbo <- wk24$CHG[wk24$TRTP == "Placebo"]
smd_tab <- lapply(trt_levels[-1], function(arm) {
  act <- wk24$CHG[wk24$TRTP == arm]
  g   <- hedges_g_hand(act, pbo)
  es  <- escalc("SMD", m1i = mean(act), sd1i = sd(act), n1i = length(act),
                m2i = mean(pbo), sd2i = sd(pbo), n2i = length(pbo))
  data.frame(Comparison = paste(arm, "vs placebo"),
             `N (active / placebo)` = paste(length(act), "/", length(pbo)),
             `Mean change (active / placebo)` = sprintf("%.2f / %.2f", mean(act), mean(pbo)),
             `Hedges' g (95% CI)` = fmt_ci(g$g, g$lower, g$upper),
             `Hand - escalc` = signif(g$g - es$yi, 2),
             `CI entirely below -0.2` = ifelse(g$upper < -0.2, "yes", "no"),
             check.names = FALSE)
})
bind_rows(smd_tab)
g_hd <- hedges_g_hand(wk24$CHG[wk24$TRTP == "Xanomeline High Dose"], pbo)
```

A negative g favours xanomeline, because a lower change means less decline.
For the high dose g = `r sprintf("%.2f", g_hd$g)`, 95% CI
`r sprintf("%.2f", g_hd$lower)` to `r sprintf("%.2f", g_hd$upper)`. The
interval includes 0 and does not lie completely below -0.2. By IQWiG's rule
the effect cannot be called even small with sufficient certainty.

## Responder analysis at 15% of the scale range

Two responder definitions follow from the threshold of `r threshold` points:
improvement (a fall of at least `r threshold` points) and deterioration (a
rise of at least `r threshold` points). In Alzheimer's disease the aim of
treatment is usually to slow decline, so deterioration is the more
informative of the two.

```{r responders}
resp <- wk24 %>%
  mutate(IMPROVE = CHG <= -threshold, WORSEN = CHG >= threshold)

resp_labels <- c(IMPROVE = "Improvement >= 10.5 points",
                 WORSEN  = "Deterioration >= 10.5 points")

resp_tab <- bind_rows(lapply(names(resp_labels), function(v) {
  cnt <- resp %>% group_by(TRTP) %>% summarise(n = sum(.data[[v]]), N = n(), .groups = "drop")
  p0  <- cnt %>% filter(TRTP == "Placebo")
  bind_rows(lapply(trt_levels[-1], function(arm) {
    a  <- cnt %>% filter(TRTP == arm)
    e  <- effect_2x2_hand(a$n, a$N, p0$n, p0$N)
    ok <- a$n > 0 && p0$n > 0        # a ratio needs events in both arms
    data.frame(Responder = resp_labels[[v]], Comparison = paste(arm, "vs placebo"),
               `Active, n/N` = paste0(a$n, "/", a$N), `Placebo, n/N` = paste0(p0$n, "/", p0$N),
               `RR (95% CI)` = if (ok) fmt_ci(e$estimate[1], e$lower[1], e$upper[1]) else "NE",
               `RD (95% CI)` = fmt_ci(e$estimate[3], e$lower[3], e$upper[3]),
               check.names = FALSE)
  }))
}))
resp_tab
```

Almost nobody improved by 10.5 points in 24 weeks, so the improvement
responder carries no information. Fewer high-dose patients deteriorated by
10.5 points than placebo patients, but the interval for the risk ratio is
wide and includes 1. Missing Week 24 values were carried forward from
earlier visits. An assessor would question LOCF, because it assumes no
further decline after a patient leaves, and would ask for a sensitivity
analysis such as the MMRM in the efficacy report.

## One table in dossier layout

A dossier summarises each endpoint in one row: patients, events, effect with
its interval, p-value and the result of the subgroup interaction tests. The
table below does this for the high dose against placebo. It follows the
order of a benefit assessment: mortality, morbidity, then side effects.

Effect measures: hazard ratio from a Cox model for time to event, risk ratio
for responders and mean difference for the continuous score. The mean
difference comes from the ANCOVA of the primary analysis, with treatment,
pooled site and baseline score. The interaction column gives the smallest
p-value of the three pre-specified subgroup tests (age group, sex, baseline
ADAS-Cog) and names its subgroup.

```{r dossier-table}
subgroup_vars <- c(AGEGR1 = "Age group", SEX = "Sex", BASEGR = "Baseline ADAS-Cog(11)")
active <- "Xanomeline High Dose"

# Smallest interaction p-value across the subgroups for any model family.
min_interaction <- function(fit_main, fit_int) {
  p <- sapply(names(subgroup_vars), function(v) {
    m0 <- fit_main(v)
    m1 <- fit_int(v)
    if (inherits(m0, "lm") && !inherits(m0, "glm")) anova(m0, m1)[2, "Pr(>F)"]
    else anova(m0, m1, test = "Chisq")[2, "Pr(>Chi)"]
  })
  paste0(fmt_p(min(p)), " (", tolower(subgroup_vars[[names(which.min(p))]]), ")")
}

# Time-to-event rows from the adverse-event sets.
ae_tte <- derive_ae_tte(adsl, adae) %>%
  left_join(adqsadas %>% filter(PARAMCD == "ACTOT", ABLFL == "Y") %>% distinct(USUBJID, BASE),
            by = "USUBJID") %>%
  mutate(AGEGR1 = factor(AGEGR1, levels = c("<65", "65-80", ">80")),
         SEX    = factor(SEX, levels = c("F", "M")),
         BASEGR = factor(ifelse(BASE <= 21, "<= 21", "> 21"), levels = c("<= 21", "> 21")))

tte_row <- function(pc, label) {
  d  <- ae_tte %>% filter(PARAMCD == pc, TRTA %in% c("Placebo", active)) %>%
    mutate(ACT = as.integer(TRTA == active), EVENT = 1 - CNSR)
  arm <- function(x) {
    km <- summary(survfit(Surv(AVAL, EVENT) ~ 1, data = x))$table
    med <- unname(km["median"])
    c(N = nrow(x), events = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", sum(x$EVENT), 100 * mean(x$EVENT)),
      median = if (is.na(med)) "NE" else sprintf("%.0f", med))
  }
  a <- arm(filter(d, ACT == 1))
  p <- arm(filter(d, ACT == 0))
  if (sum(d$EVENT[d$ACT == 0]) == 0) {
    eff <- "NE"; pv <- "NE"; pint <- "NE"
  } else {
    cx  <- summary(coxph(Surv(AVAL, EVENT) ~ ACT, data = d))
    eff <- fmt_ci(cx$conf.int[1, 1], cx$conf.int[1, 3], cx$conf.int[1, 4])
    pv  <- fmt_p(cx$coefficients[1, "Pr(>|z|)"])
    sg  <- hta_subgroups(d, pc, active, subgroups = subgroup_vars)
    i   <- which.min(sg$table$p_int)
    pint <- paste0(fmt_p(sg$table$p_int[i]), " (", tolower(sg$table$variable[i]), ")")
  }
  data.frame(Endpoint = label, `N HD` = a[["N"]], `Events HD` = a[["events"]],
             `Median HD (days)` = a[["median"]], `N PBO` = p[["N"]], `Events PBO` = p[["events"]],
             `Median PBO (days)` = p[["median"]], Measure = "HR", `Effect (95% CI)` = eff,
             p = pv, `Interaction p (subgroup)` = pint, check.names = FALSE)
}

# Mortality: deaths during the study, counts only.
dth <- adsl %>% filter(SAFFL == "Y", TRT01A %in% c("Placebo", active)) %>%
  group_by(TRT01A) %>% summarise(n = sum(DTHFL %in% "Y"), N = n(), .groups = "drop")
mort_row <- data.frame(
  Endpoint = "All-cause death", `N HD` = dth$N[dth$TRT01A == active],
  `Events HD` = as.character(dth$n[dth$TRT01A == active]), `Median HD (days)` = "",
  `N PBO` = dth$N[dth$TRT01A == "Placebo"], `Events PBO` = as.character(dth$n[dth$TRT01A == "Placebo"]),
  `Median PBO (days)` = "", Measure = "", `Effect (95% CI)` = "too few events",
  p = "", `Interaction p (subgroup)` = "", check.names = FALSE)

# Morbidity: ADAS-Cog(11). ANCOVA as in Table 4, all three arms in one model.
anc  <- lm(CHG ~ TRTP + SITEGR1 + BASE, data = wk24)
ci   <- confint(anc)["TRTPXanomeline High Dose", ]
est  <- coef(anc)[["TRTPXanomeline High Dose"]]
t4   <- readr::read_csv("outputs/t4_adascog_wk24_ancova.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot(t4$V3[grepl("^LS mean difference", t4$row_name)] ==
            fmt_ci(est, ci[1], ci[2], d = 1))   # same as the primary analysis
hdp  <- wk24 %>% filter(TRTP %in% c("Placebo", active)) %>% droplevels()
cont_pint <- min_interaction(
  function(v) lm(as.formula(paste("CHG ~ TRTP + SITEGR1 + BASE +", v)), data = hdp),
  function(v) lm(as.formula(paste("CHG ~ TRTP * ", v, "+ SITEGR1 + BASE")), data = hdp))
mean_sd <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean(x), sd(x))
x_hd  <- wk24$CHG[wk24$TRTP == active]
worse <- effect_2x2_hand(sum(x_hd >= threshold), length(x_hd), sum(pbo >= threshold), length(pbo))

morb_rows <- data.frame(
  Endpoint = c("ADAS-Cog(11) change to Week 24, mean (SD)", "ADAS-Cog(11), Hedges' g",
               "Deterioration >= 10.5 points (15% of range)"),
  `N HD` = c(length(x_hd), length(x_hd), length(x_hd)),
  `Events HD` = c(mean_sd(x_hd), "", sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", sum(x_hd >= threshold), 100 * mean(x_hd >= threshold))),
  `Median HD (days)` = "",
  `N PBO` = c(length(pbo), length(pbo), length(pbo)),
  `Events PBO` = c(mean_sd(pbo), "", sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", sum(pbo >= threshold), 100 * mean(pbo >= threshold))),
  `Median PBO (days)` = "",
  Measure = c("LS mean difference", "g", "RR"),
  `Effect (95% CI)` = c(fmt_ci(est, ci[1], ci[2]), fmt_ci(g_hd$g, g_hd$lower, g_hd$upper),
                        fmt_ci(worse$estimate[1], worse$lower[1], worse$upper[1])),
  p = c(fmt_p(summary(anc)$coefficients["TRTPXanomeline High Dose", "Pr(>|t|)"]), "",
        fmt_p(2 * pnorm(-abs(worse$yi[1] / sqrt(worse$vi[1]))))),   # Wald test on log RR
  `Interaction p (subgroup)` = c(cont_pint, "", min_interaction(
    function(v) glm(as.formula(paste("I(CHG >= threshold) ~ TRTP +", v)), family = binomial, data = hdp),
    function(v) glm(as.formula(paste("I(CHG >= threshold) ~ TRTP *", v)), family = binomial, data = hdp))),
  check.names = FALSE)

side_rows <- bind_rows(
  tte_row("TTAE", "Any TEAE"),
  tte_row("TTSAE", "Serious TEAE"),
  tte_row("TTSEVAE", "Severe TEAE"),
  tte_row("TTDCAE", "Discontinuation due to AE"),
  tte_row("TTDE", "Dermatologic TEAE")
)

section <- function(title) {
  data.frame(Endpoint = paste0("**", title, "**"), `N HD` = "", `Events HD` = "",
             `Median HD (days)` = "", `N PBO` = "", `Events PBO` = "", `Median PBO (days)` = "",
             Measure = "", `Effect (95% CI)` = "", p = "", `Interaction p (subgroup)` = "",
             check.names = FALSE)
}
as_chr  <- function(d) mutate(d, across(everything(), as.character))
dossier <- bind_rows(lapply(list(section("Mortality"), mort_row,
                                 section("Morbidity"), morb_rows,
                                 section("Side effects"), side_rows), as_chr))
knitr::kable(dossier, align = "lrrrrrrlrrr")
```

Table notes: HD = Xanomeline High Dose, PBO = placebo, NE = not estimable.
Side effects: safety population, actual treatment, time to first event,
hazard ratio and Wald p-value from a Cox model with treatment only. Values
above 1 mean more events on xanomeline. Morbidity: efficacy population,
planned treatment, Week 24 with LOCF. The mean difference reproduces
Table 4 of this repository, which the code checks. Interaction tests:
likelihood-ratio tests for time to event and responders, F-tests for the
continuous score.

Read as a whole, the table shows no clear benefit on cognition and a clear
harm on skin events and on discontinuations due to adverse events. In an
assessment that pattern would not support an added benefit. This is a
self-study on public pilot data, so the reading illustrates the method and
says nothing about xanomeline.
